messages:
Alex: Hey team — seeing intermittent 502s/timeout spikes when sending large embeddings batches. Happened ~2026-03-17 11:08 PST. Example request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d. Observed only when batch_size >= 48 and payload ~1.2MB. Billing shows charge for attempted tokens even though client got 502. Can we triage?

Maya: Sorry you're hitting this Alex. Can you paste a curl or minimal Python/JS/Go repro? Also include the exact request-id(s) and SDK versions.

Alex: Minimal curl below — reproduced reliably with 48, stable at 32:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-..." \\ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\ 
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","input":["hello"]*48}'
```
Request IDs: rq_0a1b2c3d, rq_0d4e5f6g
SDKs: python-sdk 0.9.1, node-sdk 0.8.7

Liam: Thanks. Can you also send the full response headers from a failing request (the 502) including the x-request-id returned by the API? If possible capture client-side logs and server response headers. Also try a reduced batch of 32 to confirm threshold.

Alex: Reduced to 32 works consistently. 48 fails ~30% of the time. Attached billing screenshot showing charge lines for the attempted call.

Maya: Understood — we'll collect logs. Liam, can you check ingress LB and pod restarts? Ara, runtime: any OOMs or kernel rejects for those request ids?

Liam: Quick look — no LB 5xx surge, but one worker pod restarted at 11:09. Pod logs show upstream error: "rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc=KV allocation failed" around rq_0a1b2c3d.

Ara: ResourceExhausted during KV cache alloc fits mem pressure. Can customer run a minimal repro loop and set debug to capture the full bundle? I'll post minimal SDK snippets — please run and paste stdout/stderr and x-request-id values.

Maya: Alex — please run one of these and paste the output.

Python minimal repro:
```
# python repro: run with REDWOOD_KEY env var
import os, json, requests
API_KEY = os.environ.get("REDWOOD_KEY")
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings"
payload = {"model": "embed-large-v1", "input": ["hello world"] * 48}
r = requests.post(url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}, json=payload)
print(r.status_code)
print(r.headers.get("x-request-id"))
print(r.text[:1000])
```

Node (JS) minimal repro:
```
// node repro
const fetch = require('node-fetch')
const key = process.env.REDWOOD_KEY
const body = { model: 'embed-large-v1', input: new Array(48).fill('hello world') }
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${key}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(body) })
  .then(r => { console.log(r.status); console.log(r.headers.get('x-request-id')); return r.text() })
  .then(t => console.log(t.substring(0,800))).catch(e => console.error(e))
```

Go minimal repro:
```
// go repro (run with REDWOOD_KEY env var)
package main

import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)

func main() {
  key := os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY")
  body := []byte(`{"model":"embed-large-v1","input":["hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world","hello world"]}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings", bytes.NewBuffer(body))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+key)
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  client := &http.Client{}
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err != nil { fmt.Println(err); return }
  fmt.Println(resp.StatusCode)
  fmt.Println(resp.Header.Get("x-request-id"))
}
```

Liam: Also please collect a runtime debug bundle: set REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 and attach the bundle from ~/.redwood/debug/<timestamp>.tar.gz. That bundle includes pod logs, kernel OOM events, and runtime counters.

Alex: Running Python now — got a 502 and x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d. Uploading logs in a moment.

Maya: Received logs. Initial triage: looks like the Dedicated worker hit memory guardrails and restarted, causing a failed response while billing recorded work done. Filing to infra and product for follow-up and a KB. Workaround: keep batches <= 32. :thumbsup:

DebugBot: Created incident 2026-03-17-embeddings-mempressure, assigned to eng-infra

Ara: Action items for runtime: (1) add a defensive batch-size check and return 413 with a clear billing message for oversized batches; (2) improve autoscaler mem headroom; (3) customer KB recommending safe batch sizes. I'll follow up with a PR and ETA.

Maya: Alex — thanks for verifying. If splitting to 32 removes the charge for failed attempts, confirm here and we'll prioritize the KB and runtime guard.

Alex: Confirmed splitting to 32 avoids the 502 and billing charge. Thanks everyone.
